notes.title: Major Update, Console Release, and More!
notes.content:
[h3]Hello Ground Handlers, [/h3]

Attention Steam players! We haven't forgotten about you. With [b]today's launch of the Xbox version[/b], we're also rolling out an exciting update for the PC.

First and foremost we want to apologize for our long absence. We encountered some challenges with porting to Xbox, primarily due to memory issues. The good news is, however, that we have overcome these hurdles! 

Today’s update for the PC version addresses these exact issues, as the update is focused on [b]enhancing performance for those with lower-end machines.[/b]

Before we dive into the patch-notes, have you checked out our Xbox launch trailer yet? Take a look:

[previewyoutube=yWjaqhdBSxM;full][/previewyoutube]

[u][b]PATCH NOTES: Build Version 1.4.0[/b][/u]

We are bringing some minor and major fixes that will come with release of Xbox:
[list]
[*] [b]Fixed major memory issue[/b]: Previously, each new game played didn't clear memory properly, causing memory chunks to stack up and clog the system. This could lead to the RAM running out of space and causing crashes if the game was played repeatedly without restarting. [/list]
[b]Additional:[/b]
[list]
[*] Optimized Shaders cache
[*] Optimized Static References
[*] Optimized Lighting Data
[*] Fixed Blockers: Cannot disconnect stairs when there are no passengers in the aircraft
[*] Fixed an issue where aircraft randomly drive around the taxiway during Follow Me on Warsaw
[*] Fixed broken Discord Invite link in Main Menu
[*] Corrected aircraft paths at all airports
[*] Removed collisions that were scattered on aprons at all airports
[*] Fixed Follow Me paths at Bologna
[*] Fixed an issue at parking spot 110 in Bologna
[/list]

notes.title: AirportSim DLC: Bologna
notes.content:
[b]Today marks the arrival of new content for AirportSim: the Bologna DLC! The AirportSim Bologna DLC is available now for download, priced at $9.99 / £8.50 / € 9.75 minus a 10% launch discount.[/b]

This DLC grants players the opportunity to play at an entirely new Italian airport, meticulously recreated based on photos, video materials, and documentation. But that's not all. Additionally, at the Bologna airport, we're putting into players' hands a brand-new Follow Me vehicle. This popular car, which is a hallmark of Italian airports, will allow players to experience true speed while completing tasks.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42514724/d6f18b642ad9916c5be46dccb962fec2fb58fd4c.png[/img]
Aeroporto Guglielmo Marconi was opened in 1933, meaning it has been operating for almost 100 years. Starting today, you will not only be able to admire this beautiful facility but also get to work on its premises. The DLC puts a completely new map in your hands, allowing you to experience new gameplay, either alone or with friends.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42514724/fd3cc73f554fa6d4760d0a6ad4f2306adc36ece6.png[/img]
Bologna Airport is famous for its unique Follow-me vehicle. While you might have gotten used to the comfort of the more classic pickup truck, this DLC will bring you a high-octane experience while driving this exceptional car. Get behind the wheel of a luxury sports car and see if its incredible speed will help you complete your tasks on time.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42514724/46f1a0d857b9189e6144c7c7693961612a16e024.gif[/img]

The AirportSim Bologna DLC is available now, and you can purchase it [b][url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/2727000/AirportSim__Bologna_Airport/]HERE[/url][/b]. We hope that the Italian airport will bring you a lot of joy, and you'll discover the pleasure of ground handling in the Mediterranean.

notes.title: AirportSim Patch Notes 1.2.4
notes.content:
Recently, new content has been added to the game, and we have been focussing on gathering your feedback.

Patch 1.2.4 mainly includes changes to NPC vehicles added in the last update, along with the resolution of some bugs and the addition of a few elements to improve the gameplay.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42514724/dacbcb0cb0b6e7362b923db59dffcda5667e6ce9.gif[/img]

Here's the full list of changes:
[list]
[*] Disabled collisions between unused vehicles and traffic.
[*] Added front lights to towable stairs.
[*] Introduced the option to toggle airport traffic on or off via the menu.
[*] Added audio effects for dragging and rotating a towbar.
[*] Added a plane delay icon to the tablet task list.
[*] Implemented a feature that prevents accidentally throwing cables or refueling hoses into containers.
[*] Fixed an issue where vehicle impact sounds are played when the player throws cables or refueling hoses.
[*] Added the condition that operational lights must be on during the follow-me process.
[*] Resolved an issue of passengers not climbing mobile stairs.
[*] Fixed an issue where planes skipped some path points during crossroad searching in the Follow Me task.
[*] Addressed a problem where several planes attempted to occupy a single parking space.
[*] Fixed road blockages for NPC vehicles in Warsaw.
[*] Fixed a bug where Follow Me breaks when the player restarts the game during the Follow Me process.
[/list] 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42514724/bcc2e34d6f594efbcbfcfd7b583d43f986758fac.png[/img]

We are currently working on the next update, which, in addition to fixes, will bring another new feature for you! Stay tuned for more information and feel free to join our Discord to give us feedback about this update.

notes.title: AirportSim - New Content is Here!
notes.content:
As you know, our roadmap indicates that the first milestone of 2024 has just been achieved. We are thrilled to announce that new content is here!

Today’s patch notes (1.2.3.) bring exciting new additions! Towable stairs are now available at all airports. Unlike the current TLD-ABS stairs, these need to be towed by another vehicle to be positioned near the aircraft. Players can then move these stairs around to precisely align them with the aircraft doors. Pretty exciting, huh?

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42514724/69007530333f941b703764e1e16aa3b7895386c1.gif[/img]

Also, your airports are about to become much more lively: New NPC vehicles will enhance the scenery on the single player apron of AirportSim. They will follow dedicated roads around the airport, adhere to traffic rules, stop when there is an obstacle or a player in front, and spawn in different configurations, such as tugs with or without luggage carts. Please note that these are only for visual appeal.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42514724/2d2c10940eae21dce87c589b310a765ed3619a29.gif[/img]

With this patch, several fixes are also coming:
[list]
[*] The issue of passengers not boarding the aircraft when using mobile stairs has been resolved
[*] GPU detachment from the connector in multiplayer has been fixed
[*] The range for catering connections and adding a walking path for employees to board the aircraft has been extended
[*] Multiple sound-related issues have been addressed
[*] Further improvements and fixes have been implemented
[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42514724/b8a3210a9f811ddd6dc5b93cd6d894e4bb822f3c.png[/img]

Now, put down your coffee and go check out the new features, ground handler. See you on the apron!

[*] Before the pushback task is activated, it checks if other aircraft have finished their pushback in its vicinity and if the aircraft driving on the taxiway is far enough to start the procedure. If both conditions are met, your task will become activated.

[*] Flex your creativity with the Steam Workshop: design aircraft paint skins and craft unique gameplay scenarios.
[/list]
[b]One last thing:[/b] [b]set your clocks[/b] for our release, planned for [b]5PM CET[/b] on the [b]19th of October[/b]!

The countdown has us buzzing! We're meticulously refining every aspect of the game. Also, stay tuned for an [b]exciting update about our latest partnership later this week![/b] While we're diving back into development in the meantime, if you feel we've overlooked something or if you just want to chat, leave a comment or join us on [url=www.discord.gg/airportsim]Discord[/url]!

notes.title: Development Update #4: The full list of vehicles
notes.content:
[h3]In today's Development Update, we're spotlighting our vehicles. While there haven't been significant changes since our inaugural demo, this is the first time we're unveiling the comprehensive list. Discover detailed descriptions of each vehicle below and check out our new YouTube series showcasing the specific tasks each one can handle in our AirportSim Game. Ready to explore? Let's dive in!
[/h3]

[h3][b]Refueling Truck[/b][/h3]

[previewyoutube=-UNGTCBGcL4;full][/previewyoutube]

Refueling trucks are specialized vehicles crucial for maintaining efficient and secure airport operations. Recognizing the substantial fuel needs of aircraft, these powerful machines facilitate the prompt and convenient delivery of fuel, eliminating the necessity to move aircraft to specific refueling areas.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42514724/522f3afaad0ca8430b949cfc6c159a7d5710a728.png[/img]

Read more here: 

[url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1715280/view/3709322161710375193?l=english]Refueling Truck Blog[/url]
[url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1715280/view/5301322539095092032?l=english]How to refuel an aircraft?[/url]

[h3][b]Pushback: Bison D1000[/b][/h3]

[previewyoutube=KEY1Y5PJrJ4;full][/previewyoutube]

The Bison D1000 Pushback vehicle, soon available in our AirportSim game, excels in performing pushback operations and managing aircraft repositioning on the tarmac. It ensures efficient taxiing procedures, particularly in challenging operational conditions. Part of the versatile "BISON" family, the D1000 can handle aircraft from 50 t to 600 t MTOW. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42514724/cc6f9228e02df632e702e57c77f424aa4ba9d75e.png[/img]

Read more here: 
[url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1715280?emclan=103582791472036132&emgid=3650784879029768539]
BISON: A Game-changer for Ground Handling[/url]
[url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1715280?emclan=103582791472036132&emgid=3651891124015871630]Pushing Steel Birds - With a Little Help From a BISON![/url]
[url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1715280?emclan=103582791472036132&emgid=3651907608100500054]AirportSim Mechanic Guide: Pushback[/url]

[h3][b]Pushback: TLD TMX-150[/b][/h3]

[previewyoutube=P41jRiG-KBY;full][/previewyoutube]

The TMX-150 aircraft towing tractor is meticulously engineered to execute push and pull operations on narrow and medium-bodied aircraft with a robust maximum draw bar pull of up to 12,000 daN (27,000 lbs). Its innovative design prioritizes both agility and visibility, ensuring precise and efficient operations. Upholding TLD's esteemed standards of build and component quality, the TMX-150 stands as a paragon of durability and reliability. This All Wheel Drive and All Wheel Steer aircraft tow tractor seamlessly undertake pushback and towing tasks in all weather conditions, reinforcing its role as a trusted and indispensable asset in aircraft ground handling operations.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42514724/15c643a047a85d47a64fdf4311caa8eb27a9e635.png[/img]

[h3][b]Belt Loader: TLD NBL[/b][/h3]

[previewyoutube=z5Mtrejj8OY;full][/previewyoutube]

The NBL Belt Loader stands out as a highly modular equipment, compatible with various engines and transmissions (powershift or hydrostatic). Its design prioritizes reliability and minimal maintenance costs, incorporating the latest technology and straightforward electric and hydraulic circuits for effortless servicing. The innovative boom design enables the NBL to access the lowest aircraft doorsill heights in the industry, with diverse boom dimensions available for multiple applications. Ergonomically designed, the NBL ensures optimal driving comfort, intuitive controls, and superior visibility, solidifying its position as a market leader in efficiency and convenience.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42514724/7873eff58b06abbe4faffe900635b664eafd5789.png[/img]

Read more here: 

[url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1715280/view/3651908241710640081]Belt Loader - Introducing TLD NBL[/url]
[url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1715280/view/3682298662732169511?l=english]Belt Loader - Control it better[/url]

[h3][b]Belt Loader: TG 660[/b][/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42514724/0d590799536482a9463f986573956da6a73ff732.png[/img]

The TUG 660 Belt Loader is built for reliability and performance, with a robust chassis designed for demanding ramp conditions. Its centrally mounted conveyor, adjustable at both ends, operates at varied heights for flexibility. Ensuring user-friendly operation, belt controls are accessible from both conveyor ends, and an interlock system enhances safety. The unit also features retractable conveyor guides, a collapsible safety rail, and a standard emergency hydraulic pump, underscoring its commitment to operational efficiency and safety. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42514724/7969d374906d5908b18096dc25c74c8d3bc5f303.png[/img]

[h3][b]Ground Power Unit - GPU[/b][/h3]

[previewyoutube=PEhl32yQS9I;full][/previewyoutube]

A "Ground Power Unit" (GPU) is a specialized electrical device crafted to provide power to aircraft while on the ground. Although aircraft generally rely on onboard engine generators during flight or an Auxiliary Power Unit (APU) when grounded for power, these methods expend valuable jet fuel and require manned operation. The GPU emerges as a more economical and environmentally friendly alternative, proving particularly beneficial during extended aircraft parking, like overnight stays or between rotations. By using a GPU, airports can significantly reduce fuel consumption and emissions, making it a sustainable choice for ground power supply.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42514724/ff96da051fa6fb5d39708f22031b34788be598bc.png[/img]

Read more here: 

[url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1715280/view/3683432262648325114?l=english]Ground Power Unit - Empowering Aircraft[/url]
[url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1715280/view/5320484387365996665?l=english]AirportSim Mechanics Guide: Ground Power Unit[/url]
[url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1715280/view/3637251250308875595]Powering the kings of the sky - get to know the aircraft GPU![/url]

[h3][b]Shuttle Bus[/b][/h3]

[previewyoutube=DbNt546Nzac;full][/previewyoutube]

In AirportSim, you'll have the chance to navigate the role of operating a Shuttle Bus, a key vehicle ensuring passenger contentment. This role invites you to master the art of timely and efficient passenger pickups and drop-offs. Tasked with transporting passengers to their desired destinations within the airport, your aim is to ensure a smooth, safe, and satisfactory transit experience for every traveler, enhancing overall passenger satisfaction within the airport's ecosystem. Your skill in managing these intricate responsibilities contributes significantly to the seamless operation of the entire airport, underlining the critical role of the shuttle bus in airport logistics.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42514724/ec449ec6272762424491b68db34730933037b076.png[/img]

Read more here: 

[url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1715280/view/3665415870911784935?l=english]AirportSim Mechanics Guide: Shuttle Bus[/url]

[h3][b]Tractor: TLD Jet-16[/b][/h3]

[previewyoutube=pDxDTM6COmY;full][/previewyoutube]

The Jet-16 stands out as an electric-powered tractor meticulously designed to amplify speed and comfort in airport operations. Its creators have triumphed in focusing not just on exceptional performance but also on unparalleled comfort, a claim we've had the honor to validate firsthand. Recognizing the extensive hours airport workers spend daily within this vehicle, utmost priority has been given to its interior design. The Jet-16 ensures it offers optimal comfort and ergonomic support, epitomizing a perfect blend of efficiency, comfort, and thoughtful design, ensuring it is not just a vehicle but a comprehensive experience for its operators.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42514724/b7032569a4d163f7df84014e4bf0272b7fd80ead.png[/img]

Read more here: 

[url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1715280/view/3651904437098960754]Jet - 16: The Universal Soldier[/url]

[h3][b]Tractor: TG MT[/b][/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42514724/4faa9e0f8226fb9829d592b5b5bac4d306a324ab.png[/img]

The TG MT Tractor (TUG MT) is a robust and reliable solution for efficient aircraft towing and maneuvering within airport environments. Designed for optimum performance and operator comfort, it ensures swift, smooth, and safe handling of various aircraft types, enhancing overall ground support operations and ensuring timely flight schedules.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42514724/c64d822508ed63c43a400242edb10823f55dd5ce.png[/img]

[h3][b]TLD JCT-60 “Mulag”[/b][/h3]

[previewyoutube=2DsFSwcNPHw;full][/previewyoutube]

The JCT-60 TLD Tractors are robust 6-ton GVW tow tractors designed for optimal cargo handling and pushback in demanding industrial environments. With a substantial drawbar pull of 4500 daN (10,116 lbf), they ensure powerful performance. The heavy-duty single-piece chassis guarantees durability and resistance to harsh conditions. The tractors prioritize operator comfort with a spacious, ergonomic driver’s station and efficient suspension, ensuring excellent maneuverability and ease of use. The JCT-60 tractors stand out for their blend of high performance and low maintenance, reflecting a commitment to reliability and operational efficiency.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42514724/91fe0d9be6e4e1ab15a54177055c480b96ba077f.png[/img]

[h3][b]Jetway[/b][/h3]

[previewyoutube=WXgpMo9GQqY;full][/previewyoutube]

Embarking on an aerial journey is a thrilling experience, further enhanced by the use of jetways. These engineering masterpieces, also known as aerobridges or passenger boarding bridges, have transformed the process of boarding and deplaning from aircraft, elevating the overall travel experience. The integration of jetways into airport infrastructure signifies an unwavering commitment to passenger convenience, safety, and accessibility, underscoring their indispensable role in modern aviation.

[b]Warsaw Chopin Jetway[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42514724/59fe0a140e550b74acad31e3657708bf76d447d9.png[/img]

[b]Keflavik Airport Jetway[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42514724/fc60446af9dee0235b9263a8990aa4ba8cb28b47.png[/img]

[h3][b]Catering Truck[/b][/h3]

[previewyoutube=4aBSIwv-Gok;full][/previewyoutube]

A hungry passenger is often an unhappy passenger. ;) In the game, the catering truck plays a vital role in ensuring passengers are satisfied and well-fed during their flights. It is efficiently used for swift and seamless delivery of food onboard the aircraft. In the bustling environment of a busy airport with stringent schedules, the catering truck's expedited and efficient service is paramount. Its elevated container feature facilitates direct loading to the aircraft, eliminating the need and time for manual carriage up the stairs, thus ensuring timely and effective service.

notes.title: Development Update #3
notes.content:
[h3]Welcome to the third episode of our Development Update series. In this episode, we'll delve into the [b]features and mechanics[/b] that have evolved since our first demo. As you may have already heard, our release date is set for 19th October 2023, so you'll soon be able to explore everything firsthand! In this update, we'll touch upon changes on the apron as well as vehicle-related aspects. However, our primary focus will be on mechanics, as there will be an upcoming episode dedicated entirely to vehicles. Let's dive right in.[/h3]
[h3]
[b]New Mechanics in Baggage Handling on Keflavik & Warsaw[/b][/h3]

At major airports, such as those in Warsaw and Keflavik, luggage handling systems stand out not just in terms of size and scale but also in their advanced equipment.

[previewyoutube=2XmP87a-aFQ;full][/previewyoutube]

Consistent with our design philosophy, our game airports are meticulously modeled on their real-world counterparts, replicating both their look and functionality. Whenever a flight is prepped for departure, suitcases materialize on specialized carts. These carts glide along a rail system suspended from the ceiling. An advanced computer system allocates specific spots on conveyor chutes, each identified by a unique number. Digital screens at each chute display the relevant flight number, directing where the suitcases should be dispatched. These are then collected by the in-game crew (the player) and loaded onto the designated aircraft. For chute number details, players can consult their in-game tablet by selecting the appropriate plane number.

[previewyoutube=4J-hcDH9nkI;full][/previewyoutube]

Interestingly, at larger airports, baggage claim coincides with where luggage is offloaded from the plane to the terminal. However, passengers here retrieve their bags from a standard conveyor system.

[h3][b]Incorporating Cargo Interiors into Both Aircraft[/b][/h3]

[previewyoutube=AKes7zvHtls;full][/previewyoutube]

From our earlier materials and our inaugural demo, players might remember that luggage was automatically received. Upon interaction with the crew, it was sequentially set on the pre-prepared loading belt. Following valuable feedback from our community and internal deliberations, we've revamped this process. Our aim in AirportSim is to authentically represent the tasks of ground handlers, especially since baggage management is integral to their role.

[previewyoutube=w_vyP0FRQ2c;full][/previewyoutube]

With our updates, the real challenge begins once the cargo doors swing open. For unloading, players must venture inside the hold to retrieve every piece of luggage. During the loading phase, when dealing with a significant volume of bags, careful and strategic arrangement is essential to ensure everything fits neatly.

[h3][b]Bypass Pin Introduced for Both Aircraft[/b][/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42514724/59b8b17ea57d17eff7454593f77507d074c24fd2.png[/img]

In our initial demo, once the aircraft landed, users were tasked with deploying cones and positioning wheel chocks to stabilize the plane and enhance safety. Recognizing the importance of comprehensive safety measures, we've incorporated an additional feature: the bypass pin. Now, as you ensure the aircraft's security and gear up for pushback, attending to this crucial detail is a must.

[h3][b]Enhanced Gate Door Animations[/b][/h3]

[previewyoutube=GltWpmGyYa4;full][/previewyoutube]

In AirportSim, we give paramount importance to passengers. From the 2.0 version of our initial demo, players can observe passengers seamlessly exiting the terminal through beautifully animated gate doors, a feature that's consistent across all airports.

We recognize the profound impact of intricate details in providing a richer gaming experience. These nuances immerse players deeper into the game's realism. Now, rather than passengers merely appearing near the doors, they're brought to life with a complete animation that showcases them walking through the doors as they open.

[h3][b]Introducing Stackable Cones[/b][/h3]

[previewyoutube=t6vIxkxtqjQ;full][/previewyoutube]

In our debut demo, players were limited to handling just one cone at a time, a restriction that considerably prolonged the task. With our newest update, players can now efficiently stack up to five cones and subsequently place them either individually or collectively on the ground.

[h3][b]Draggable Trolleys Feature Introduced[/b][/h3]

[previewyoutube=HCBsAmiPuW8;full][/previewyoutube]

Since updating the trailers in our recent demo to include a steerable front axle, we recognized the necessity for manual trolley maneuverability. Players can now intuitively grip the trolley's frame to pull it, emulating real-world practices. This enhancement streamlines the process of linking multiple trailers together.

[h3][b]Introducing Fresh Aircraft Liveries[/b][/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42514724/b5c4eb65e1a262738666a313449d3bc5fd7e2be1.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42514724/790ec2cef745a02ca2db57f2d523fd09c3e57f84.png[/img]

Airports without planes are unimaginable; they truly are the heart and soul of such locations. With that in mind, we've been steadfast in our commitment to ensuring our aircraft not only look impeccable but also enhance the game's diversity. Over recent months, we've rolled out a spectrum of new liveries: from authentic brands like Wizz Air and Atlantic to our playful creation, "Luftwaffles", and even designs birthed from our community contest. And rest assured, this chapter on liveries is far from closed!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42514724/0de5dad39d606dc84c76da18b115e26944e531f5.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42514724/c5e220090ee63d9c16b9aea20dc1cdcb361feaf2.png[/img]

[h3][b]Scenario Editor Feature[/b][/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42514724/a19b436c1bc5a484520926ead895772867a85ca7.png[/img]

We've introduced a versatile scenario editor, empowering players to craft custom flight schedules tailored to their preferences. With intuitive airport maps at their fingertips, players can seamlessly designate parking spots for aircraft. The editor breaks down tasks between arrivals and departures, while offering a wide selection of airplanes and their liveries—encompassing both official designs and those integrated via the Steam Workshop. Furthermore, players can customize elements such as the date, time, weather conditions, and specific airports.

[h3][b]Make Your Custom Aircraft Liveries[/b][/h3]

Leveraging the templates we've furnished, players can craft their very own distinct aircraft liveries. They have the freedom to share these creations with fellow players via the Steam Workshop. For offline enjoyment, they can simply slot them into the designated game directory. These bespoke liveries are compatible with custom scenarios and will be showcased on free-roaming aircraft. In the multiplayer setting, if a participant has an identical livery, it will be visible to them. Conversely, if they lack the host's specific livery, one from their existing collection will be chosen at random for display.

[h3][b]Tablet Features [/b][/h3]

[previewyoutube=YePwR-OQ6LA;full][/previewyoutube]

Besides the functionalities you're already familiar with on our tablet, we've introduced a camera flight mode and a fast-travel option directly to vehicles.

Now, as mentioned in our introduction, let's briefly discuss the changes in mechanics and features for our vehicles.

[h3][b]Your favorite - Pushback[/b][/h3]

[previewyoutube=ISYr21zak8k;full][/previewyoutube]

We recognize that a comprehensive pushback feature in AirportSim was a significant concern for many. Rest assured, we've included it in its entirety. Understanding the importance of aircraft pushback for players, we've diligently crafted this feature to offer a genuine experience. Your responsibilities encompass preparing the vehicle, connecting to the aircraft, and guiding it to the specified location. Additionally, virtual teammates are on hand to help ensure safety during this process.

[h3][b]Passengers and mechanics related to the Shuttle Bus, Jetway, and Stairs.[/b][/h3]

[previewyoutube=WZjWd-gGUkw;full][/previewyoutube]

In the most recent demo, you can firsthand experience the intricacies of passenger handling, a multifaceted procedure that demands a range of tools. At present, you can trial the stair mechanics. It's not only about accurately positioning them on the tarmac, but also adjusting them to the right elevation. Only once they're securely docked can you ascend and access the aircraft doors—and don't overlook the safety handrails! This location often serves as a rendezvous point for the Shuttle Bus. 

If there's a significant distance between the terminal and the aircraft, this vehicle provides a secure transportation method for passengers. Within the game's framework, it's your responsibility to ensure every passenger is seated and departs the bus after their journey, and always be mindful of the doors. Alternatively, you can utilize the Jetway. When choosing this method, you need to meticulously connect it to the plane, enabling passengers to leave without having to venture far from the terminal.

[h3][b]You Can Be a Marshall[/b][/h3]

[previewyoutube=aCdnvtLUFmo;full][/previewyoutube]

If you've tuned into our live streams, you've seen marshalling in action. As aircraft touch down, they're going to need your guidance. Your role? Ensure pilots navigate accurately, bringing their planes safely to the designated spot. We've added a touch of authenticity with a distinct stop marker, showing you exactly where each aircraft should halt.

[h3][b]Catering Truck[/b][/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42514724/f4a13f0d467208321c1776ec869e9e9a13baed82.png[/img]

The catering vehicle is designed to replenish an aircraft's onboard supplies. It's not just about driving; positioning the truck at the specified location on the airport tarmac is crucial. Once firmly in position, you can then raise the loading platform to the right height and seamlessly link up with the aircraft for the restocking process.

[h3][b]Ground Power Unit (GPU) Exploration[/b][/h3]

[previewyoutube=1NyblVjOEV4;full][/previewyoutube]

We're excited to present two unique Ground Power Units for your hands-on experience in the demo version. Though each unit has its distinct features, their operational and handling procedures remain strikingly similar. Once you've positioned the unit appropriately, it's essential to establish a connection with the aircraft. With a proper link, you can activate the unit using specific controls. Additionally, it falls upon you to communicate to the aircraft's crew the operational status of the GPU—whether it's activated or deactivated.

[h3][b]Follow Me[/b][/h3]

[previewyoutube=TW1njKWw5ag;full][/previewyoutube]

In AirportSim, players dive right into their tasks shortly after an aircraft touches down. The "Follow Me" vehicle plays a crucial role in safely guiding the aircraft to its designated spot on the airport grounds, effectively averting any potential chaos on the tarmac. Assuming the role of a player, you step behind the wheel of this vehicle, charting the course towards the predetermined aircraft location, all while ensuring that the pilot closely follows your lead.

[h3][b]Luggage[/b][/h3] 

[previewyoutube=YltRtTeJizY;full][/previewyoutube]

Handling baggage has undergone significant changes from the initial version, where baggage appeared to "teleport" to and from the aircraft. Based on your feedback, we've overhauled the mechanics related to baggage. Now, you have direct access to the aircraft's cargo hold, where you must personally load and unload baggage. We believe this modification will greatly enhance the immersion when playing AirportSim.

[h3][b]Securing aircraft[/b][/h3]

Securing aircraft on the airport apron has been a part of our journey since the very first demo. However, as you can observe while playing the latest version, we haven't been resting on our laurels. We've enhanced the functionality of wheel chocks, ensuring they now respond correctly. Furthermore, we've streamlined your work by enabling you to collect multiple chocks simultaneously. One noteworthy addition is the By Pass Pin, which was mentioned earlier in the text—a highly significant safety feature that we've decided to incorporate into the game.

[h3][b]Refueling[/b][/h3]

[previewyoutube=gyI510erbdk;full][/previewyoutube]

Refueling is an entirely new mechanic that you haven't had the chance to explore in detail yet. It's a complex procedure, so it might pose a challenge initially. Once you've positioned yourself on the apron, the responsibility falls squarely on your shoulders. You should begin by connecting the equipment to the aircraft's power source before proceeding to pump the aviation fuel. Keep a close eye on the fuel quantity and ensure everything is securely in place when you complete the entire process.

notes.title: BISON: A Game-changer for Ground Handling
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42514724/41ac550df12579503730d44b458850be75fd0ca7.png[/img]
The airport apron is a busy, dynamic environment, teeming with ground crew, vehicles, and machinery. Amid this orchestra of activity, a select few vehicles stand out, not just for their functions but for their sheer excellence. One such vehicle is the Goldhofer BISON. Loved by ground handlers and now making its appearance in the our AirportSim game. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42514724/1ed8ad67e020c5c9002a0d32a8a237cbdb8bd52f.png[/img]

[b]What is the Bison's function?[/b]

On the airport apron, the Goldhofer BISON operates as a dedicated tow tractor. Its primary roles encompass pushback operations from terminal gates, aircraft repositioning within the tarmac—including transfers between hangars and gate assignments—and ensuring efficient taxiing procedures. This is particularly crucial in sectors where utilizing aircraft reverse thrust or powerback maneuvers would be operationally challenging or pose safety risks.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42514724/891d5af9c7769f847549e540c8d47c2007c7831a.png[/img]

[b]Ergonomics[/b]

Ground crew members spend hours operating vehicles, and ergonomics is paramount.
The BISON is a pleasure to operate. The cockpit is sophisticated yet intuitive, ensuring the driver's comfort is at the forefront. This, coupled with a spring-suspended cabin, provides an unparalleled view, making it easier for the operator to navigate the busy airport terrain. Additionally, the well-maintained cabin air conditioning ensures the driver remains at ease during extended shifts. And for those longer shifts? The BISON is ahead of the game with its large diesel tank and advanced "IONMASTER" technology and design of the cab gives the driver 360 degrees of vision, which contributes to safety.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42514724/9c8bbe968c499d07e3c51d16745a2d1aca995d7e.png[/img]

[b]Reliability[/b]

When we discuss reliability, the BISON stands tall. Crafted with robust and durable components from quality manufacturers, it's designed for the long haul. A defining feature is its carry-over part strategy, allowing seamless operations across the entire BISON family. Furthermore, its adaptability shines through, thanks to a flexible ballasting concept which ensures the vehicle is ready for changing conditions.It is worth mentioning that Bison can work in very extreme temperatures of -30°C or the blistering heat of +52°C, the BISON operates seamlessly, evident by its usage on every continent.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42514724/e70b231467bee14f72172401c4f41ccc6147b681.png[/img]

[b]Safety[/b]

Safety, a paramount concern on any apron, is deeply ingrained in the BISON's design. Its ergonomic handling ensures reduced damage, leading to fewer repairs and cost savings. A clear view of the couplings directly from the cabin and a safe single-man operation are testaments to its meticulous design. With flexible driving modes, including all-wheel, front-wheel, and crab steering, the BISON truly offers a driving experience like no other.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42514724/2a2417846b5e77c8dcb961b635797a8eda1cbe86.png[/img]

[b]Maintenance [/b]

In terms of diagnostics and maintenance, the BISON is again in a league of its own. Error messages and information are displayed in plain text in its multifunction display, simplifying troubleshooting. The time-saving operations, combined with 1,000-hour maintenance intervals, optimized hydraulic systems, and a lubrication-free drive shaft, all underscore BISON's commitment to long-term use with minimal hassle.

The "BISON" D 1000 is particularly notable. This unstoppable powerhouse can tow hefty aircrafts like the Boeing 747-400 or Airbus A340-600, weighing up to 400 t (880,000 lbs) MTOW.

[b]Experience the BISON D1000 in AirportSim[/b]

AirportSim offers players a chance to operate the legendary Goldhofer BISON D1000. This vehicle effortlessly tows aircraft like the Airbus A320neo or 737 MAX. So, if you're ready to jump into the world of airport operations, grab the BISON's steering wheel and get pushing because those planes won't move themselves!

notes.title: AirportSim | Development Update #2 | Airports
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42514724/3055a4e24b58641dc09396dec8e71fe886b64e8b.jpg[/img]
[h3]Welcome to our Development Update #2. In this edition, we will focus on the airports where you can take on the role of a ground handler in AirportSim. Primarily, we will be discussing the visual enhancements rather than the gameplay mechanics. Let’s take a closer look at the modifications made since the February demo and explore the new features.[/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42514724/b76fe308bba65397fa8c2e9f2f475663f16475e5.png[/img]
[h3]Refinements and enhancements to terminal buildings across all airports.[/h3]

Significant upgrades have been made to the airport buildings to align them more closely with their real-world counterparts, coupled with substantial visual enhancements.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42514724/a5bbb9863f94c03f2aa7d955cf38e2be6c271e2d.png[/img]
[h3]Presenting Key West Airport![/h3]

Following the release of the demo version, we nearly completed three airports: Vagar, Keflavik, and Warsaw. As per the AirportSim plan, upon launch, you will be able to engage in gameplay at four airports. It's time to unveil the missing fourth one - Key West Airport! It might have already appeared in some articles and screenshots, but for those who haven't encountered it yet - welcome!

We began, of course, by gathering materials in the form of videos, photos, and building plans. Next, we transitioned to modeling all the buildings and surroundings. After extensive work on accurately reflecting the airport, we shifted our focus to the gameplay. We incorporated aircraft paths, vehicles, and distinctive minor elements of the airport, which help to capture the "essence" of the location.

The airport is now complete, as you can frequently observe during our weekly community streams. We hope that you will appreciate the American airport and dispatch many planes from sunny Florida.

For more information about the airport itself, please refer to the article we prepared for you some time ago [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1715280/view/3682298662750626263]LINK[/url].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42514724/26b163932e24ad0aeb05549c6e3834d08080ae64.png[/img]
[h3]New Terminal Interior at Vagar & Key West[/h3]

Our goal, as always with simulators, is to achieve the most realistic effect possible. Therefore, we have redesigned the interior of the Vagar & Key West  terminal to make it as comparable as possible to the original. We have also made minor modifications to the gameplay at Vagar, details of which can be found in the next section.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42514724/81f35180fe3fdb6bf14e9c867ad3e4e6959d2490.png[/img]
[h3]Repair of Luggage Collection and Drop-off Points at Vagar[/h3]

The luggage collection and drop-off points in our game were previously placed in reverse order compared to reality. We have corrected this mistake, so you will be able to play the correct way at the premiere. It's a small change, but a satisfying one!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42514724/79648969017cf7827b5518580de9b8ffd4844a39.jpg[/img]
[h3]New Jetway Model at the Warsaw Chopin Airport[/h3]

Warsaw Airport is a place that demanded a significant amount of our effort and attention. As you may be aware from our previous updates, we regularly visit this place, so accurately recreating it is a point of pride for us. While you have already seen the jetways at Keflavik in our materials, and can now examine them in the new demo, they differ from those in Warsaw.

We decided that each airport should have jetways that mirror their real-life counterparts. This necessitated a meticulous examination of every detail. During one of our visits, the staff demonstrated the precise functioning of the jetways, and based on the photos and videos we captured, we were able to adapt our existing models to fully replicate the appearance of the ones in Warsaw.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42514724/4f40aac403d95eadd64403276833f24e2839e592.jpg[/img]
[h3]New Support Vehicles: Firetrucks and Ambulances for Every Airport[/h3]

Airports are, in many ways, like organisms where every component has a vital role to play in the overall function. You will take on the role of apron staff, but it's important to remember that there are also people dedicated to ensuring health and safety. We are committed to accurately replicating real airports in the game, which is why it is essential to include crucial vehicles like ambulances and firetrucks. Although you won't be able to assume the roles of a paramedic or firefighter, their presence will undoubtedly enhance the game's immersion. You will have the opportunity to observe this vehicles closely during gameplay.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42514724/d1af7099f79d96bae4549defa9444baf2312ccb0.png[/img]
[h3]Luggage Sorting Area at Warsaw Airport[/h3]

What we, as non-ground handlers, see at the airport is only part of the picture. There are restricted areas inaccessible to those without proper authorization, one of which is the luggage sorting area.


Thanks to our collaboration with Warsaw Chopin Airport (Yes, we mentioned it today a lot of times, but we are just really thankful for them.), we were granted access to this area, enabling us to accurately replicate it, both visually and functionally.


Airports facilitate the travel of hundreds of thousands of people, and along with them, their luggage, which must be sorted and dispatched on the correct flights. Playing AirportSim allows you to see what this space truly looks like, as it has been recreated based on photos, recordings, and our own visits. Additionally, the sounds you hear during gameplay were recorded by us, adding to the realism and immersion of the experience.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42514724/793ef47b097535c2b9129599a707fb47f5684abe.png[/img]
[h3]Added General Aviation Aircraft at Key West Airport - Light Aircraft[/h3]

We are committed to enhancing the immersion of our game in various ways. Although Key West is a smaller airport compared to Warsaw or Keflavik, it has its own unique characteristics. The airport is predominantly used by small aircraft, a detail we have chosen to emphasize in our game.


While navigating the airport apron or during your work, you will notice the light aircraft that we have incorporated, located in a specially designated area behind the fence. We believe this addition enriches the charm of this beautiful airport, and for those of you who are aviation enthusiasts, it will provide an opportunity to closely observe these aircraft and, of course, heighten the sense of realism and authenticity of being at an actual airport.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42514724/b85947be94ece57aefc4a0851d718e59c7d5fcd1.gif[/img]

And... that concludes today's development update. We sincerely hope you appreciate the changes and the effort we are investing in the development of AirportSim for its full game release. For those who missed the initial series of Development Updates, you can find them here: [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1715280/view/3683434708706413893]Link[/url]. Now, we encourage you to try our new demo and stay tuned for more exciting updates!


Additionally, we invite you to join our [url=discord.gg/airportsim]Discord[/url] channel, where you can engage in discussions about the game, aviation, and provide us with your valuable feedback on the new demo.

notes.title: AirportSim | Development Update #1 | Graphics
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42514724/af30e1972b295d6593ce02b370efa9d10520785e.gif[/img]

[h3]Greetings, ground crew! We are excited to extend an invitation to our inaugural development update. It has been a while since we embarked on the AirportSim game development journey, and much has evolved, especially when compared to the demo you have the chance to experience. [/h3]

Crafting high-quality, fully optimized, and meticulously detailed real-life vehicles and interiors is no small feat. Today, our spotlight is on graphic enhancements, animations, and visual transformations that have been in progress since the March release of the latest demo. Let's discover the changes together! 

We kindly suggest grabbing your favorite drink and some snacks, as this is going to be an extensive update brimming with details. 🍿🥤

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42514724/f15dbfdd086ba69bedb6c492cc976a7052ef8bf3.gif[/img]

[h3]Updates and visual corrections to B737 aircraft[/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42514724/e4e87eb1d5beeb4466ea7f257a70275492fa5ead.gif[/img]

Airplane models are among one of the most crucial elements in the game, thus we dedicate considerable attention to their creation. In recent weeks, we have been meticulously reviewing our B737 model to make the final adjustments. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42514724/b291e4b13be3ba8fcc86073f54253a8e536d281d.gif[/img]

This aircraft draws inspiration from a real airplane, and during the game's production, we identified certain inconsistencies. It became evident that it incorporated elements from various airplanes, necessitating a thorough reevaluation of photos and drawings to address these discrepancies. At present, following the implemented changes, it embodies a highly realistic model.

[h3]Introducing the Airbus A320 NEO and further improvements [/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42514724/293c648aae0706b7b09eb6edac29e6327a5d880f.png[/img]

In the AirportSim demo 2.0 version, you were introduced to one of our aircraft. However, our ambitions extended beyond just that initial offering. Following the demo's launch, we embarked on a journey to introduce an entirely new and officially licensed model: the Airbus A320 NEO. This particular aircraft model is widely recognized and immensely popular. Understanding the fervent anticipation surrounding its inclusion, we approached this endeavor with unwavering professionalism right from the outset.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42514724/a7e8e296072ea68a6efd929bdb788e98fb01cd0a.gif[/img]

Our first step involved an in-depth study of the documents and technical specifications graciously provided by Airbus Company. This rigorous preparation allowed us to immerse ourselves in the technical intricacies, ensuring that no surprises awaited us during the production process. In addition to relying on photographs and videos, we were fortunate to witness the aircraft in person, affording us the chance to meticulously scrutinize vital details that might have otherwise evaded us.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42514724/37801a9d9e06d788e9770dd6b3be0e9a68be094f.gif[/img]

With this thorough understanding, we transitioned into the digital realm. Methodically crafting the aircraft model, we entrusted the next phase to a skilled 3D animation specialist. Each aircraft possesses its own distinctive attributes, including its operational mechanisms. Navigating tasks like connecting GPUs and manipulating cargo doors demanded a complete reimagining, but the ultimate outcome promises a remarkably authentic portrayal of piloting this machine.

[h3]Improving Aircraft Taxiing Movement, landing and take off animation[/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42514724/a5d80258530f4d16d950d2ac919d4455438c1761.gif[/img]

Our work mainly involves observing airport operations, ground handling processes, and aircraft – not only when they're up in the sky but also when they're on the ground. Sometimes it feels like we're airport detectives, investigating what's happening both in the skies and on the ground.

Once planes touch down, they each have their own unique way of behaving. Additionally, every airport has its own set of taxiing routes, which play a crucial role in maintaining safety and order during various activities.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42514724/b41286fa9e8e48e68edccf5ea29ca5aa40b4eb2d.gif[/img]

We've taken steps to improve the way aircraft move around on the airport apron, making their behavior more realistic. Currently, they follow designated paths, and the animations run seamlessly without any glitches or frame loss.

[h3]Stair Animation Correction for TLD ABS 580[/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42514724/fc7e18ad3ce04fccfdbeb469bbc1351d24598f3e.png[/img]

When developing a game, especially a simulator as intricate as our AirportSim, which is meticulously crafted based on real equipment, it's virtually inevitable to completely eliminate errors. Following the demo's release, we identified an issue with the TLD ABS 580 – its hydraulic actuator was positioned inaccurately. A disappointing discovery, perhaps? But here's the silver lining: our dedication shines through!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42514724/1fd1a6c65ae42fcc3af768fb3b2027d71d39f3a5.gif[/img]

Although we were confident in the precision of the vehicle's design, it was thanks to a message from one of our players that we caught onto this subtlety. We genuinely value all the feedback we receive and, as a result, swiftly recognized the inaccuracies within the vehicle's construction.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42514724/9bac521100be71d8d68bc04856569b118f498a26.gif[/img]

Without hesitation, we resolved to set things right. Through meticulous rectifications and texture refinements, the vehicle now impeccably mirrors its real-life counterpart, epitomizing our commitment to delivering an exceptional experience.

[h3]Aircraft Texture Overhaul and Further Enhancements[/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42514724/12afa60fe9ff954ee6863a5affc9682afd60bad0.png[/img]

This one's going to be a short one. We've revamped textures to enhance their user-friendliness for crafting liveries, and we've also made minor adjustments to rectify a handful of visual issues that emerged under specific lighting conditions.

[h3]Jet engine exhaust visualization has been rectified[/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42514724/e5341d31cb4a7a9a38118c7e894a3a351c1b6c91.png[/img]

After unveiling the demo, we meticulously reviewed every aspect, seeking ways to not only enhance its functionality but also elevate its visual appeal. During a visit to an airport, our team members noticed a distinct feature – the engines appeared more conical in shape compared to those in AirportSim. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42514724/40d0ac73bdaae004b1bc47bc4de7c2ba65e7d7be.png[/img]

With this observation in mind, we decided to refine their appearance, giving them a sleeker, conical design that adds to their overall allure. Players who experienced the demo will certainly spot the difference between these engines and the ones showcased in the final version.

[h3]Rectification of Passenger Front and Rear Door Animation for B737[/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42514724/24430bc3993c6b0e00e8f157e84209d75e3c4817.gif[/img]

Airplane doors are often something passengers have the chance to closely observe. They are technologically intricate, requiring comfort and safety. Balancing these two aspects isn't simple for designers, as we discovered during our in-depth study of their operation. We've introduced modifications that will readily catch the attention of keen observers. In tandem with the seamless engine performance, we've made subtle refinements that enable players to genuinely witness the realistic operation of airplane doors.

[h3]Button Animation on Conveyor Belt Cars[/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42514724/920fe728ea5fcc84f04c2ecf4093f4b87aeefa6a.png[/img]

Our Belt Loaders have undergone a remarkable transformation, and we're brimming with pride about the changes we've made. In the world of airport operations, efficiency reigns supreme, which is precisely why equipment needs to be incredibly versatile. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42514724/99c35b0d0357283a26c1256e7f6736e70aeed76a.gif[/img]

These vehicles, equipped with conveyor belts, are typically operated by skilled drivers. But here's the ingenious twist – we've integrated meticulously designed external control panels. These panels eliminate the need for drivers to constantly return to the vehicle for belt adjustments or changes in orientation.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42514724/b438d9c3acb3c4fa0e489c6fb6688162c64b318b.gif[/img]

Now, let's talk about the game itself. We've meticulously reimagined these vehicles to offer external control, complete with dynamic animations that illustrate the seamless use of buttons. This enhancement goes a long way in creating a truly immersive experience for players when they're in charge of these machines.

[h3]Corrections to Global Lighting and Weather Systems
[/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42514724/d1f87a8619a9be3eecc98a83222e902d18ea26be.gif[/img]

As gamers, we often overlook one of the most crucial elements in a game: the weather and time of day. Starting the same scenario under different weather conditions offers us a remarkably different gameplay experience. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42514724/d8e552accd1d347b036a09c161ca860d98ed48b1.png[/img]

These conditions play a pivotal role in shaping the narrative. We've implemented numerous changes, particularly focused on refining these factors, with an emphasis on enhancing the weather dynamics. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42514724/2320a9ce6ed919cb1381cfc9b20d15cb098834ea.png[/img]

Rain, for example, now exhibits a remarkably realistic appearance. Moreover, you'll notice how light interacts with puddles, adding a new level of immersion. We've also meticulously adjusted the sun's position in relation to the airports, ensuring it faithfully mirrors the real-world sun's placement based on the in-game time of day.

[h3]Summary[/h3]

In summary, this development update has been a thrilling ride. From perfecting aircraft models to elevating animations and textures, every detail has been meticulously refined. Our dedication to realism shines through, whether it's in the intricacies of engine exhaust or the controls of conveyor belt cars. We've also fine-tuned weather systems and lighting to deepen the immersion. As we unveil these enhancements, we're excited to have you experience the enhanced AirportSim. Feel free to ask any questions – let's continue the journey together! And of course... Remember to wishlist us! 😉

Now we are preparing ourselves for Gamescom 2023, as you may have noticed – we will be there!

notes.title: AirportSim Mechanics Guide: Pushback
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42514724/7bb8bbea6052ebbd156e0cf5231f854941b8c36d.gif[/img]

Indeed, we are all familiar with pushback procedures in real life! But what specific features in AirportSim support this functionality? Read this article carefully and let's delve deeper into the topic, starting from the basics… The task involves expertly maneuvering the plane from its stopping point onto the taxiway.

[b]The task is universal and applies to all types of vehicles
[/b]
1. Parking the vehicle with a towbar at the designated location.
2. Conducting a walkaround by the player to ensure everything is properly secured.
3. AI Supervisor attaching the headsets and wingwalkers take their position near the wings
4. Player attaches the towbar to the main gear.
5. Waiting for pushback clearance and releasing brakes - activating Logo + Position lights.
6. Granting pushback clearance, releasing brakes - the aircraft activates the Beacon lights upon clearance.
7. Commencing pushback. 
8. Communicating the possibility of engine start-up - pilot confirmation (starting engines 1 and 2 sequentially).
9. Stopping the aircraft
10. AI Supervisor disconnecting the pushback from the aircraft.
11. Departure of the pushback vehicle.
12. Once the player moves away, the aircraft activates the Taxi Lights and begins taxi to the runway.
 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42514724/10e26019d7e4cb5783754622864ae7e6ca7181f6.gif[/img]

After the pushback is finished, wait for the AI Supervisor to disconnect the Towbar and then reattach it to the pushback vehicle itself. Only then can the player move away from the taxiway. Next, the AI takes the ByPass Pin, disconnects the headsets, and closes the GPU flap. The player must then park the vehicle and the towbar in the designated spot.

Remember that during pushback, you need to cooperate with the Wing Walker and the Supervisor. They maintain communication with the aircraft crew and ensure safety on the apron during aircraft towing. Working at the airport is a team effort!

[b]Reaching the Conclusion[/b]

As you may have observed, the pushback process and all the activities involved to execute it efficiently are quite complex. This text aims to simplify the process for you in the future. Our game offers various pushback vehicles, including Goldhofer Bison, AirportSim Custom Vehicles, and, in future updates - a vehicle without a towbar. notes.title: Ground Power Unit - Empowering Aircraft
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42514724/3da636e2943469c3f39460a72df05e9b8884f0d1.png[/img]

As the aviation industry continues to soar to new heights, the efficiency and safety of aircraft are not solely reliant on their in-flight capabilities but also on the seamless ground operations that support their functionality. Among the many pieces of ground support equipment utilized in airports worldwide, one stands out as a crucial component in ensuring smooth aircraft operations - the Ground Power Unit (GPU). In this article, we delve into the electrifying facts about GPUs in the airport ecosystem.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42514724/7dcd10d57c04f8cbcaa995595cb1bc5f1b130483.png[/img]

[b]What is a GPU?[/b]

A "Ground Power Unit" or "GPU" is an electrical device designed to supply aircraft with power while they are on the ground. During flight, aircraft typically receive electrical power from onboard generators within the engines or through an Auxiliary Power Unit (APU) when grounded. However, both of these methods consume jet fuel and necessitate manned aircraft operation. The GPU offers a more cost-effective and eco-friendly alternative, especially when aircraft are parked for extended periods, such as overnight stays or between rotations, helping to conserve fuel that would otherwise be consumed by the APU.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42514724/bb5979f4ea368067287ea84477548a4938833b42.png[/img]

[b]Electrifying Facts About GPUs[/b]

One distinguishing feature of GPUs lies in their ability to deliver a "ripple-free" or "clean" voltage, ensuring the protection of sensitive avionics and control systems within the aircraft during maintenance and engine starting operations. While the standard household power supply delivers 110/220 volts and 50/60Hz, aircraft require distinct power specifications. Larger airliners demand power at 115 volts and 400Hz electrical frequency, whereas smaller aircraft, like business jets, rely on a 28 Volt DC power supply.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42514724/e1a80d2bf07551b72a690957e8fd8ea68a6eb010.png[/img]

[b]Types of GPUs and Functionality[/b]

GPUs come in various configurations to cater to the diverse needs of different aircraft and airports. Some GPUs are powered by conventional engines running on petrol or diesel, while others utilize advanced battery technology. Additionally, some GPUs operate as solid-state converters that don't generate electricity but instead convert the airport's utility power supply to the specific frequency and voltage required by the aircraft.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42514724/7e8f633b00ebdffef146085d43359934336ad0cf.png[/img]

[b]The Need for Aircraft Ground Power Units (AGPUs)[/b]

The importance of AGPUs becomes evident when an aircraft lands and is parked at a designated aircraft stand. While in flight, the aircraft's electrical power requirements are fulfilled by the jet engines, which also act as power plants to supply electricity to critical and auxiliary systems. However, once the aircraft reaches its stand, it is no longer safe or practical to keep the jet engines running due to the ground staff's activities around the aircraft.

During this phase, the aircraft still requires electrical power for various essential functions. These include keeping aircraft lights on for cleaning purposes, energizing cockpit and cabin systems, and facilitating passenger embarkation and disembarkation. AGPUs play a vital role in providing the required electrical power to ensure a seamless transition between flights and maintain safety and efficiency during ground operations.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42514724/9206886d4e68e1302e9eb55cd5acf9cf9514198c.png[/img]

[b]Conclusion[/b]

The Ground Power Unit (GPU) is a remarkable piece of ground support equipment that plays a crucial role in the aviation industry. By supplying clean electrical power to parked aircraft, GPUs help conserve fuel, reduce emissions, and ensure the safety of sensitive avionics during maintenance and engine start-ups. notes.content:

As you may have noticed, one of the vehicles you'll be able to play in AirportSim is the Shuttle Bus. There's nothing more challenging than ensuring passenger satisfaction! Let's take a closer look at how it will be implemented in our game:

[b]Receiving a summons [/b]
The tablet will provide graphic and audio notifications.

[b]When can you start? [/b]
The task becomes feasible once the stairs can be connected to the aircraft (cooperation is possible when multiple players are involved).

[b]Bus stop [/b]
Depending on the available space, the bus will stop in front of the left wing, precisely at its left edge. This designated area will be highlighted in yellow, indicating where you should stop. It's a predefined location.

[b]Boarding passengers onto the Shuttle Bus [/b]
After parking and opening the doors, passengers will begin to disembark from the aircraft. The aircraft information display will show the percentage of passengers already loaded onto the vehicle.

[b]Don't forget to close the doors [/b]
Once all the passengers have been loaded, the player closes the doors and heads towards the terminal. Each airport has its own designated stop, marked by a specific zone where the player should park.

[b]Letting passengers off [/b]
When the bus doors open, passengers will exit, and the number of passengers inside the vehicle will be displayed. Once the passenger count reaches zero, the doors can be closed, and the bus can be moved to its designated location.

[b]The same process in reverse [/b]
Picking up passengers from the stop and transporting them to the aircraft will follow the same procedure.

[b]Bus stop (pickup and drop-off) [/b]
The bus stop is a designated location on the map, serving as a fixed point for picking up and dropping off passengers, regardless of the flight.

Similar to the fuel truck, the parking spot for the bus will be marked by a rectangular area. Single pickup request: If there is only one passenger pickup request at that time, using the tablet will not be necessary.

notes.title: AirportSim Mechanics Guide: World of Airport Marshals
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42514724/2ea321cf8504720282daed96bd0d9bb1313bc6e2.gif[/img]

[b]Introduction[/b]

Airport marshals are some of the most recognizable workers on the airport tarmac. Sporting their vibrant yellow jumpsuits, they are commonly referred to as "marshals" or known by the phrase "follow me." Let's delve into the fascinating world of airport marshals and discover some fun facts about their role in ensuring smooth operations.

[b]Guiding Aircraft to Their Parking Slots[/b]

After landing, marshals skillfully guide the aircraft to their designated parking positions using a series of hand signals. While they have a wide range of signals at their disposal, they typically rely on a core set of 10. These signals convey important directions for taxiing, engine start-up or shutdown, and braking.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42514724/23ee439225b3c326ac000dd5458b8d3b7c61bd93.gif[/img]

[b]The Multi-Faceted Role of Airport Marshals[/b]

Airport marshals have diverse responsibilities beyond guiding aircraft to parking spaces. They conduct thorough Foreign Object Debris (FOD) inspections, ensuring a safe runway environment. They also manage airport facilities and coordinate with various professionals for efficient operations. Their role extends far beyond guiding planes, making them indispensable to airport functionality.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42514724/5c20f52b34f0cacd323822389d581ba2e19ce916.gif[/img]

[b]Unique Marshal Vehicles[/b]

One of the distinctive features of airport marshals is their "follow me" vehicles. These specially designed cars, prominently displaying the phrase "follow me," ensure clear visibility in all weather conditions. However, it's worth noting that not all marshal vehicles are the same. Some airports have taken a creative and luxurious approach, featuring Lamborghinis in Bologna and Porsches in Hannover. It's safe to say that these marshals certainly know how to make an entrance!


[b]Time for the Most Important Marshal in AirportSim[/b]

In our AirportSim game, you have the opportunity to step into the shoes of a marshal and experience the real-world challenges of ground handling. Your tasks will include securing the parking area by removing objects and vehicles, directing the aircraft to the correct parking spot, assisting with precise alignment during parking, and responsibly operating the Follow Me vehicle.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42514724/81ab4696ced9b26fde8ab07dcf53fa7d9032f067.gif[/img]

[b]Going to Conclusion[/b]

Airport marshals play a vital role in guiding aircraft, ensuring safety, and maintaining order on the airport tarmac. Beyond their signature yellow jumpsuits and "follow me" vehicles, they contribute to various operational aspects of an airport. Next time you're at an airport, keep an eye out for these vibrant marshals who keep things running smoothly and add a splash of color to the aviation world. And if you're up for the challenge, soon you will have the opportunity to join the AirportSim game to become the ultimate marshal!

Working at an airport requires a lot of precision, and time is crucial. The team working on the airport apron has various equipment to assist with tasks related to aircraft, but is there something that helps with time management? In the game AirportSim, we have prepared a special Tablet for you, which will be with you at all times, enabling you to quickly and efficiently handle your tasks. But is that all?


Aside from being a simulator, AirportSim is also a computer game, so it's important for us to ensure smooth and satisfying gameplay alongside realism. That's why we have come up with and introduced the tablet, which will be your right-hand companion and eliminate the need to step away from "work" to check something or make changes.

Time and Weather Control

We strive to provide an immersive experience while playing, so there's no need to change these settings in the game options. Simply use the device, which is your main assistant during gameplay.


[b]Map[/b]

The airport is constantly bustling, and during intense gameplay, it's easy to lose track of what's happening. That's where the map function comes in. At any moment, you can use it to examine the placement of aircraft and your own position, allowing you to plan your next actions accordingly.

Knowing when a particular aircraft needs to depart and when the next ones will arrive is crucial for airport staff, and thanks to the tablet, you'll have all the information at your fingertips.


[b]Tasks[/b]

When the airport is less busy, you can manage without assistance, but what about when there are more aircraft? Each arriving plane presents multiple tasks, which can be overwhelming during high traffic. Here again, the tablet comes to your aid. It provides an overview of ongoing operations, allowing you to double-check what needs to be done for each specific aircraft at any given moment.

notes.title: Jetways: Enhancing Air Travel Experience and Airport Efficiency
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42514724/6ed972440ab1494468e512f8e6bdd24357322183.png[/img]

Embarking on a journey through the skies is an exhilarating experience, made even more delightful by the presence of jetways. These marvels of engineering, also known as aerobridges or passenger boarding bridges, have revolutionized the way we board and deplane from aircraft. Join us as we explore the captivating world of jetways, unveiling their fascinating features and the numerous benefits they bring to passengers and airports alike.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42514724/92ff3f821047926daa3203cd2e60601042c9e858.png[/img]

[b]Evolution and Origin: Bridging the Gap[/b]

Step back in time to 1958, a pivotal moment in the history of air travel. At Chicago O'Hare, the first Aero Gang Plank Boarding Bridge was tested, unveiling the very first jetway and forever transforming the way we embark on our aerial adventures. Gone were the days of tarmac walks; the jetway emerged as a sophisticated and enclosed walkway, bridging the gap between passengers and aircraft.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42514724/76920bd17f62e0916d7615156170d9e72e3ff390.png[/img]

[b]Passenger Comfort and Convenience: A Passage of Delight[/b]

Picture yourself entering a jetway, and a world of comfort awaits. These ingenious aerobridges prioritize passenger well-being, offering a controlled environment like no other. With air conditioning, heating, lighting, and even Wi-Fi connectivity, these walkways transform the boarding and deplaning process into a seamless and pleasurable experience. Some jetways even offer a panoramic view through their glass walls, allowing passengers to immerse themselves in the beauty of the aircraft and its surroundings.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42514724/39269cb54e9c93775632953aa626e203eb981e66.png[/img]

[b]Flexibility and Adaptability: The Ever-Adjusting Corridors[/b]

Jetways are masters of adaptation, capable of accommodating aircraft of various sizes and types. Connected to the airport terminal by flexible corridors, they extend and retract effortlessly, reaching the aircraft's doors with grace. This remarkable flexibility empowers airports to efficiently handle a wide range of planes, ensuring smooth operations and seamless transitions.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42514724/3ad669291ff874fb1fa921486fd68ede5d136c19.png[/img]

[b]Safety Measures: A Steady Passage[/b]

Safety is of paramount importance in the realm of jetways. As you traverse these enclosed walkways, sturdy handrails guide your way, offering a reassuring grip. Non-slip surfaces ensure surefooted steps, regardless of weather conditions. Equipped with emergency lighting, jetways stand ready to navigate through low-light situations, ensuring passenger security and peace of mind.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42514724/9c54a44df2255e9afa133b00f0a5da0957226a0c.png[/img]

[b]Streamlined Operations: Efficiency at its Finest[/b]

Jetways play a pivotal role in streamlining airport operations. By providing a dedicated pathway for boarding and deplaning, they minimize turnaround times between flights. This efficiency enhances overall airport capacity, reducing delays, and leaving passengers with more time to embark on their journeys with ease.

In conclusion, jetways have transformed air travel, bridging the gap between passengers and aircraft. They prioritize comfort, adapt to different planes, ensure safety, and streamline airport operations. Jetways are an indispensable feature of modern airports worldwide, enhancing the journey to the skies. So, next time you walk through a jetway, take a moment to appreciate the engineering marvel that elevates your travel experience.

notes.title: AirportSim Mechanics Guide: The GPU vehicle
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42514724/7a9ef240d52f3d0922e447873721fb41f567cd11.gif[/img]When playing our game, AirportSim, you will have the opportunity to operate various ground handling vehicles, including the GPU vehicle. Let's begin with a brief explanation of what the GPU vehicle is.

In the game, the GPU (Ground Power Unit) vehicle serves as a power generator that supplies electrical power to stationary aircraft or helicopters, enabling the starting of their engines. This power source can also be utilized for servicing and maintenance tasks. The GPU power unit can either be stationary or mobile, mounted on a cart or a vehicle. To connect the GPU to an aircraft, an appropriate electrical cable with a standard plug is used, which connects to a socket hidden in the aircraft's fuselage or front landing gear compartment.

In AirportSim, players can experience the challenging task of operating the GPU vehicle. As part of the game mechanics, you will be responsible for connecting and disconnecting the GPU from the aircraft. Here is a step-by-step guide for this process

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42514724/c90b0784f192d2f2c63745742769fad70dd02606.gif[/img]

Connection

1. Turn on the Engine Power switch (this will illuminate the green Engine Start LED).
2. Press the Engine Start button to initiate engine start-up and increase the engine's RPM.
3. Wait for 60 seconds for the oil temperature to reach 80 degrees Celsius (number 9) and the engine temperature to reach 150 degrees (number 10).
4. Connect the GPU cable to the aircraft.
5. Switch the ENGINE knob to the RUN position (this will increase the engine's RPM).
6. Set the DC OUTPUT switch to ON.
7. Signal the flight crew that GPU is running and APU is ready to be turned off

Disconnection and GPU shutdown:

1. Signal the flight crew that they should start up the APU
2. Set the DC OUTPUT switch to OFF.
3. Set the ENGINE knob to IDLE (this will decrease the engine's RPM).
4. Disconnect the GPU cable from the aircraft.
5. Turn off the engine by setting the Engine Power button to OFF (this will shut down the engine).

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42514724/492ebf60004d70f3286e3396a3eba8e17e1d31f7.gif[/img]

By following these mechanics in AirportSim, players can master the operation of the GPU vehicle and successfully power aircraft engines while enjoying the immersive gameplay experience.

notes.title: Follow Me: The unsung hero of the airports
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42514724/b1e37ad9ab781755838ef845d979ee174030821d.png[/img]

If you have ever flown into a busy airport, you might have seen a car with a bright yellow or orange livery driving around the apron, with a large “Follow Me” sign on top. These cars are used to guide aircraft around the taxiways, from the runway to the parking spot, and are an essential part of airport operations. In this article, we will take a closer look at the Follow Me cars and their role in ensuring safe and efficient aircraft movement on the ground.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42514724/5b84afd3597a303a2c125fcebd1f57fb186b8713.png[/img]

The primary function of a Follow Me car is to guide aircraft from the runway to the parking area, or vice versa. When an aircraft lands and taxis to the runway exit, the Follow Me car driver receives instructions from the air traffic controller to guide the aircraft to the designated parking spot. The driver positions the car in front of the aircraft and uses hand signals to guide the pilot. This process is particularly helpful in low visibility conditions, such as fog or heavy rain, where pilots may have difficulty seeing the taxiway markings.

Follow Me cars are equipped with a variety of features that make them well-suited for their role. On top of the car, there is a set of antennas that receive messages from the air traffic control tower, allowing the driver to communicate on airport frequencies. The driver also controls the Follow Me sign on the roof of the car, which is used to signal to the pilot where to go. Additionally, the car has extra-bright lights mounted on the roof or hood to illuminate the taxiway or runway during nighttime operations.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42514724/cae56464b5b800816150724bbac6a52951def0f4.png[/img]

Inside the car, the driver has access to a dashboard with associated switches and a traffic screen that allows them to send and receive messages from dispatch and listen to the given clearances. The car also comes equipped with standard safety equipment, such as a fire extinguisher and wheel chocks, to ensure the safe operation of the aircraft.

Follow Me cars are not just helpful for pilots, but also for ground crews and airport staff. When an aircraft arrives, the Follow Me car can guide it to the correct parking spot, ensuring that other aircraft can move around the apron unimpeded. Additionally, the cars are used during safety inspections of the runway, taxiways, and other areas, ensuring that any hazards are identified and addressed promptly.

In conclusion, Follow Me cars play a critical role in the safe and efficient movement of aircraft around airports. They are equipped with a range of features and functions that make them well-suited to guide pilots during takeoff, landing, and taxiing. Whether you are a passenger, a pilot, or a ground crew member, the Follow Me car is an unsung hero of airport operations, making your journey smoother and safer.

notes.title: From Gagarin to Concorde: The Impact of Human Space Flight on Aviation
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42514724/760b706468feb2b5b5805092fdc380d9bb86f055.jpg[/img]

[b]Today marks the 62th anniversary of Yuri Gagarin's historic orbit of the Earth - an event that not only opened the doors to human space exploration, but also had a significant impact on the aviation industry.[/b]

In the early 1960s, aircraft were still the primary mode of transportation for long-distance travel. However, the race to space between the United States and the Soviet Union had a profound impact on the aviation industry, particularly in the development of faster and more advanced aircraft.

Gagarin's historic flight inspired a renewed focus on developing supersonic passenger jets that could travel at speeds of up to twice the speed of sound. The most notable of these was the Concorde, a joint venture between British Aerospace and France's Aerospatiale that was capable of flying from London to New York in just over three hours. The Concorde was seen as the pinnacle of aviation technology at the time, and its development was partially driven by a desire to keep up with the rapid advancements being made in space exploration.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42514724/98631db7c364edbfc2d79240379dbd82e627523f.png[/img]

But the impact of human space flight on aviation extends beyond just the development of faster aircraft. Many of the technological and scientific advancements made in space exploration have also been applied to aviation, particularly in the area of safety.

For example, advanced materials developed for spacecraft have also been used to improve the safety and durability of aircraft. Better navigation systems and weather forecasting have also been developed thanks to advancements in space technology.

Moreover, the intense training and preparation required for space travel have also had an impact on aviation safety. Astronauts undergo rigorous physical and mental training to prepare for the demands of space travel, and this same level of training and preparation has been adopted in the aviation industry to ensure the safety of pilots and passengers alike.

So while the achievements of human space flight are truly remarkable, they also have a ripple effect on other industries - including aviation. The innovations and advancements made in space exploration have helped shape the aviation industry into what it is today, and it's a testament to the human spirit of exploration and innovation.
